 Judgment

The petitioners have filed this Petition under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of SCCH-25 Rs.61,20,000/- for the Death of Sagar K.T. in a road traffic accident dated 21.06.2020.

2. The case of the Petitioners' in brief is that:
On 21.06.2020 at around 6.30pm, the deceased along with his friends and family members were returning home to Bangalore from Ramanagara.
On that day deceased was driving the Swift Car bearing No.KA-53-MD-4572 in a slow manner and was proceeding by following all the traffic rules.
When they reached near Kallugopahalli Mysore - Bangalore main Road, all of a sudden due to unintentional circumstances the Swift Car skid and toplled upside (turned turtle).
Due to terrible impact the deceased suffered severe fatal injuries and died on the spot.
The Bidadi Police have registered a Criminal case against the driver of the Swift Car bearing No.KA-53-MD-4572 In Cr.No.170/2020.
The said police have sent the body of the deceased to the Rajarajeshwari Hospital for postmortem.
The Doctors of the said hospital have conducted the SCCH-25 Postmortem and opined that death was due to head injury sustained by him.
3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, the deceased was working as a Driver and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
He was the only bread earner of the family and contributing entire amount towards maintainance of the family.

On account of sudden death of the deceased, petitioners have Thammaiah vs Rohini M.A on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57407466/
2 lost their only source of income.

The objections of the 1st respondent:
She has denied the entire claim petition except admitting that she is the owner of the Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MD-4572.
The car was insured with the 2 nd respondent and it was valid from 10.08.2019 to 09.08.2020.
The policy was valid as on the date of accident.

Further denied the manner of accident and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
6.
The objections of the 2nd respondent:
It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-MD-4572.
It has contended that the petition is not maintainable for non compliance of Sec.134 and 158 (6) of MV Act.
It has contended that the complaint was lodged against the deceased.
It would clearly indicate that the deceased himself was solely SCCH-25 responsible for the alleged accident.
Further contended that the deceased did not have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, occupation, income of the deceased and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioners proves that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Sagar K.T.?
2. Whether the Petitioners proves that, the deceased sustained injuries by use of vehicle bearing No.KA-53-MD-4572 in the accident and succumbed to the said injuries?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom payable 4.
What Order or Award?

Accordingly, the Tribunal holds that the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are father, mother and elder sister of the deceased Sagar K.T.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
The petitioners have filed this petition u/Sec.164 of the MV Act.
However, Sec.164 of MV Act has come into effect only after 01.04.2022 and since the date of accident SCCH-25 is 21.06.2020, the applicable provision is 163-A of MV Act.

Under these circumstances the petitioners need not prove the rashness or negligence on the part of the offending vehicle but it is sufficient if they prove the occurrence of the accident by involvement of the vehicle resulting in injuries and death of the deceased.
In support of their case the petitioners have got examined the second petitioner as PW.1 who has reiterated the petition averments.

13. Further, it is pertinent to note that in a petition filed under Section 163-A of MV Act, the question to be considered by the Tribunal is the involvement of the vehicle against which the compensation is sought for and not whether there is rash or negligence on part of the rider/driver of the vehicle against which the compensation is claimed.
The aspect of negligence has no role whatsoever to decide question of the entitlement for compensation.

17. In the case of 'United India Insurance Vs. Sunil Kumar and Another' the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under;
"........in a proceedings under Section 163-A of IMV Act it is not open for the insurer to raise any defence or plea of negligence on the part of the victim".

entities.text: United India Insurance Vs. Sunil Kumar and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, in para No.8 of the said judgment, it is clearly observed by Hon'ble Apex Court that, "... it is clear that grant of compensation under Section 163-A of the Act on the basis of the structured formula is in the nature of final award and the adjudication there under is required to be made without any requirement of any proof of negligence of the driver/owner of the vehicle/s involved in the accident.
This is made explicit by Section 163(a)(2).

Though the aforesaid Section of the act does not specifically exclude the possible defence of insurer based on the negligence of the claimant as contemplated under Section 140(4), to permit such defence to be introduced by the insurer and or to SCCH-25 understand the provision of Section 163A of the act to be contemplating any such situation would go contrary to the very legislative object behind introduction of section 163A of the act,
namely final compensation with a limited time frame on the basis of the structured formula to overcome situation where the claims of the compensation on the basis of the fault liability was taking an unduly long time.

In fact, to understand the Section 163-A of the act to permit the insurer to raise the defense of negligence would be to bring a proceeding under section 163A of the act at par with the proceedings under section 166 of the act which would not only be self contradictory, but also defeat the very legislative intention."

18. In view of above provision of law and case laws, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under Section 163-A of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal.
All that has to be considered by this Tribunal is whether vehicle against which the claim made is involved in the accident.
In this case, it is pertinent to note that nowhere in the written statement the Second Respondent has denied the involvement of Car bearing Reg.No.53-MD-4572 in the accident.

The Chargesheet was filed against her son.

sentences.text: Claim cannot be filed against insurance company independently of the insured.
SCCH-25 24.
A perusal of policy makes it clear that there was third party coverage and personal accident coverage for the owner.
In the case on hand, it is an admitted fact that the deceased was not the owner of the Car.
Such being the case, he cannot be covered under personal accident coverage.
The deceased was driving the car that met with the accident and so he is not even a third party to the policy.
Since he was driving, he cannot be considered as an inmate of the Car.
On the other hand, as per the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ningamma's case, he steps into the shoes of the owner of the vehicle.
It is already a settled principle of law that the owner is liable to pay compensation u/Sec.163-A of MV Act and he cannot be the claimant as well as the recipient.

The liability of the owner and the insurer is joint and several under the policy and when there is no liability on the Thammaiah vs Rohini M.A on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57407466/
9 owner, there can be no liability on the insurer.

Under these circumstances the petitioners need not prove the rashness or negligence on the part of the offending vehicle but it is sufficient if they prove the occurrence of the accident by involvement of the vehicle resulting in injuries and death of the deceased.
13. Further, it is pertinent to note that in a petition filed under Section 163-A of MV Act, the question to be considered by the Tribunal is the involvement of the vehicle against which the compensation is sought for and not whether there is rash or negligence on part of the rider/driver of the vehicle against which the compensation is claimed.
The aspect of negligence has no role whatsoever to decide question of the entitlement for compensation.
18. In view of above provision of law and case laws, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under Section 163-A of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal.
All that has to be considered by this Tribunal is whether vehicle against which the claim made is involved in the accident.
In this case, it is pertinent to note that nowhere in the written statement the Second Respondent has denied the involvement of Car bearing Reg.No.53-MD-4572 in the accident.
Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.8, this court is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to involvement or use of the Car bearing No:KA-53-MD-4572 in the accident and in that the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries.
They have pleaded that due to the accidental injuries their son deceased Sagar K.T. died on the spot.
According to the Petitioners, the deceased was working as a Driver and earning sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Age of the deceased 22.
These are a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
A perusal of policy makes it clear that there was third party coverage and personal accident coverage for the owner.
In the case on hand, it is an admitted fact that the deceased was not the owner of the Car.
Such being the case, he cannot be covered under personal accident coverage.
The deceased was driving the car that met with the accident and so he is not even a third party to the policy.
Since he was driving, he cannot be considered as an inmate of the Car.
It is already a settled principle of law that the owner is liable to pay compensation u/Sec.163-A of MV Act and he cannot be the claimant as well as the recipient.
The liability of the owner and the insurer is joint and several under the policy and when there is no liability on the Thammaiah vs Rohini M.A on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57407466/
9 owner, there can be no liability on the insurer.
Under these circumstances, since the petition u/Sec.163-A is itself not maintainable, the SCCH-25 petitioners are not entitled to any compensation.
